newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: GOLF-NZ SPORT-Gow leads in clubhouse, Long best NZer.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NZ SPORT-Gow leads in clubhouse, Long best NZer.

text.p: PARAPARAUMU BEACH, Dec 5 - Sydneysider Paul Gow was the early clubhouse leader in the first round of the New Zealand Open at Paraparaumu Beach Golf Club on Thursday, NZPA reported.
Gow carded a five-under-par 66 in light winds and warm conditions that were leaving the course open to good scoring this morning.

He came to life with an eagle two at the 286m par-four sixth hole before adding a birdie at the par-five 12th and then signing off with back-to-back birdies at the par-four 17th and par-five 18th for a bogey-free round.

Gow shares the top spot on the leader board with New Zealander Michael Long whose birdie on the sixth took him to five-under after 15 holes. Also at five under was Victorian Mark Allen, who was burning up the course with six birdies and one bogey after 12 holes.
Wellingtonians Stephen Scahill and Marcus Wheelhouse are three-under, both after 12.

Scahill, who recently qualified for the European Tour, began the day with two birdies before suffering a triple-bogey at the 383m par-four third. However he held his game together well to respond with birdies at the fourth,
Among other leading players on the course, Greg Turner was two-under after 13 holes, Michael Campbell was square after 12 and playing partner Peter Senior of Australia was one-under.
Safely in the clubhouse at three-under was Martin Peterson of Sydney, the brother of well-known Australian amateur Lester, with four birdies and one bogey.
